summary: Derived valuation metrics from Polymarket 'closing market cap above $X' YES prices. Each 'above $X' market is a separate order book, so raw midpoints are arbitrage-adjusted (volume-weighted isotonic regression) into a monotone CDF before any metric is computed. Raw values are preserved alongside the adjusted ones. Two output tiers are kept strictly separate: TIER 1 (derived.market) are pure market transforms with no assumptions; TIER 2 (derived.scenarios) require external inputs and each carries a sourced, dated, ranged assumption (see assumptions.json). A scenario with no usable assumption renders 'input_required', never a fabricated number.

isotonic_adjustment.method: Volume-weighted Pool Adjacent Violators (PAVA) enforces a non-increasing CDF across thresholds. On a violation (an earlier P(>X) below a later one), adjacent markets pool to their volume-weighted mean, pulling the estimate toward the more liquid quote. Each market stores raw_prob and adjusted_prob; all metrics use the adjusted curve.
assumptions: Weight = market volume (fallback 1 when volume is unavailable, e.g. price-only history).
isotonic_adjustment.sensitivity_note: Removes negative-probability artifacts that arise because the markets are not jointly arbitrage-constrained. Per-snapshot monotonicity_violations and max_adjustment are published.

implied_median.method: Threshold where the adjusted CDF P(cap > X) crosses 0.50, by linear interpolation.
assumptions: Monotone adjusted survival curve (guaranteed by isotonic adjustment).
implied_median.sensitivity_note: Robust: depends only on the two thresholds straddling 50%.

median_band.method: Spread-implied uncertainty on the median (live only): the best_bid and best_ask curves are each isotonic-adjusted, each one's 0.50 crossing is taken, and the median is bounded by { low: min, high: max } of the two. null when no two-sided book exists (price-only history).
assumptions: Bid/ask quotes are present for enough thresholds to cross 0.50; missing quotes are excluded, never synthesized.
median_band.sensitivity_note: Converts the point median into a defensible range; width reflects book tightness.

implied_mean.method: Bucket-weighted expected value over the adjusted distribution; tails use midpoint offsets (base case: lowest - 0.15, highest + 0.40).
assumptions: Below-lowest midpoint = lowest - 0.15 ($T).
Above-highest midpoint = highest + 0.40 ($T).
Within-bucket mass at the bucket midpoint.
implied_mean.sensitivity_note: Assumption-sensitive; a sensitivity range is published (see mean_sensitivity).

mean_sensitivity.method: implied_mean evaluated over a 3x3 grid of tail midpoints (below in {0.10,0.15,0.20}, above in {0.30,0.40,0.60}); reported as { central (base case), low (grid min), high (grid max) }.
assumptions: The grid spans plausible tail placements.
mean_sensitivity.sensitivity_note: A tight band proves the mean is robust to tail assumptions; a wide band discloses fragility.

iqr.method: p25/p75 valuations = adjusted CDF crossings at 0.75 and 0.25 (the 50% confidence band).
assumptions: Monotone adjusted survival curve.
iqr.sensitivity_note: Robust interpolation; null when a bound lies outside the quoted range.

bucket_prob.method: adjusted P(> this) - adjusted P(> next); top bucket = adjusted P(> top); a '< lowest' bucket = 1 - adjusted P(> lowest) completes the distribution.
assumptions: Computed from the adjusted (monotone) curve, so every bucket is >= 0 and all buckets sum to 1.0 (asserted at build).
bucket_prob.sensitivity_note: No modelling assumptions beyond the isotonic adjustment.

confidence.method: Worst-of several signals, each producing a human-readable reason: active-threshold count, monotonicity adjustments (count + max magnitude), mean bid/ask spread, thin-liquidity breadth (share of markets below a volume floor), and anomalies (inputs identical to prior snapshot, markets closed/not accepting orders, total volume far below the trailing 7-day median). Tier is capped at 'medium' for price-only history.
assumptions: high: >=12 thresholds AND 0 adjustments AND mean spread < 0.04 AND deep books AND no anomalies.
medium: 8-11 thresholds, OR <=2 adjustments, OR spread 0.04-0.08, OR 20-50% thin, OR price-only, OR a flagged anomaly.
low: <8 thresholds, OR >2 adjustments, OR spread > 0.08, OR >50% thin, OR multiple closed markets.
confidence.sensitivity_note: Liquidity breadth is not assessed when volume is unknown (price-only history).

material_adjustment.rule: An isotonic (monotonicity) adjustment whose maximum magnitude is below 0.5% (MATERIAL_ADJUSTMENT = 0.005) is treated as IMMATERIAL: the reliability tier stays 'high' with a 'negligible monotonicity tweak(s)' reason instead of dropping to 'medium'.
material_adjustment.rationale: A violation pooled to a sub-0.5% tweak is float-level quote noise, not a data-quality defect; penalizing it would over-penalize and make the tier oscillate on negligible price adjustments. Larger adjustments still tier down by count (<=2 -> medium, >2 -> low). Near settlement the carve-out applies instead (pinned rungs manufacture large apparent violations structurally).

windowed_volume_floor.rule: The 7-day-volume path to a HIGH liquidity tier (7d >= $200K) additionally requires 24h volume >= $2K (VOL24_HIGH_FLOOR). Absent 24h data counts as 0.
windowed_volume_floor.rationale: Without the floor, a STALE one-week-old volume spike on a now-dormant market (24h ~ dead) read HIGH on activity that no longer exists — the red-team F1 finding of the 2026-06-30 calibration pass.

book_depth_selection.rule: derived.liquidity.book_depth is the DOMINANT-outcome leg's resting-order depth — the leg the headline number rests on, proxied by the most-traded leg (highest all-time volume) — with a max-across-legs fallback only when the leader leg has no book data.
book_depth_selection.rationale: The initial Increment-C selection (MAX per-leg, as described in the 1.7.0 changelog entry below) over-credited a market whose deepest book sat on an obscure low-volume longshot rather than the headline: the wrong direction for a trust signal. Corrected by red-team finding F1 (2026-06-30); this entry supersedes the 1.7.0 changelog's 'max per-leg' wording.

raw_sha256.method: sha256 over the canonical JSON serialization of raw_inputs (fixed key order: token_id, threshold, midpoint, best_bid, best_ask, volume; ascending by threshold; literal API string values). Unchanged from 1.0.0 so archived snapshots remain verifiable.
assumptions: Consumers re-serialize the stored raw_inputs identically to reproduce the hash.
raw_sha256.sensitivity_note: Provenance check: proves derived numbers came from the stored, unaltered inputs. Status flags (closed/active) are deliberately excluded from the hashed inputs.

categorical.method: A categorical event (named mutually-exclusive outcomes, e.g. 'How many Fed rate cuts in 2026?') is N Yes/No legs whose YES midpoints form a PMF. Each outcome's displayed probability is the leg's YES midpoint NORMALIZED so the distribution sums to 1 (de-vig: the market-maker overround is removed). Consensus = normalized Shannon entropy over the outcomes (0 = one outcome certain, 1 = uniform). Dominant outcome = the largest normalized probability.
assumptions: Legs are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (a valid PMF).
categorical.sensitivity_note: HASH RECIPE (same as every kind): raw_sha256 is over the RAW observed YES midpoints in raw_inputs (synthetic threshold = leg index for a stable canonical sort), NOT the normalized probabilities. Normalization is a display transform only — the hash is over truth, not presentation.

placeholder_filter.rule: Before de-vig normalization, PLACEHOLDER legs are removed: a leg is an artifact only when it has ZERO all-time volume AND (a generic '<word> <letter>' label such as 'Candidate C', OR a midpoint still pinned within 0.02 of the 0.5 untraded listing default). Any traded leg (volume > 0) is always kept; a zero-volume leg with a genuinely divergent quote (a real long-shot) is kept too. If filtering would remove every leg, the original set is used unchanged.
placeholder_filter.rationale: Polymarket seeds categorical events with 25+ untraded generic legs at ~0.5 each; including them in the de-vig denominator collapses the real leader (a true ~97% leader read 7%). The filter applies to the DERIVED display PMF only — every observed leg still lands in raw_inputs and the hash.

exclusivity_guard.rule: Before any de-vig, each categorical board is classified: INSUFFICIENT_OUTCOMES (fewer than 2 placeholder-filtered priced real legs — one or zero real outcomes cannot form a distribution); else NESTED_DEADLINE (>=2 legs worded by/before <date> covering >=80% of placeholder-filtered legs, with >=2 distinct deadlines and raw probabilities non-decreasing by deadline within 2.5pp, cross-checked against gamma per-leg endDates — a disagreement lands AMBIGUOUS); else EXCLUSIVE when the placeholder-filtered raw sum is in [0.8, 1.25]; else NON_EXCLUSIVE. Only EXCLUSIVE boards are de-vig normalized. Guarded boards display RAW observed prices with every PMF-dependent derivation suppressed (entropy, dominant outcome/probability, consensus strength, implied winner, the consensus reliability lift) and carry derived.exclusivity { verdict, basis, headline? }; a NESTED board’s headline is its longest-horizon raw probability.
exclusivity_guard.rationale: The de-vig presumes mutually-exclusive outcomes. 31% of live categorical boards are nested deadlines (a cumulative curve in time) and others are independent multi-binaries; normalizing them FABRICATES probabilities (live proof: a nested board priced at 20.5% raw displayed as 49%, its 62% chance of no-event erased). A single priced real leg is the same fabrication in miniature: normalizeProbabilities([0.30]) === [1.0], reading a 30% market as a certain winner (preventive fix, 2026-08-03 — zero live instances at fix time). Misclassification is asymmetric by design: every wrong verdict degrades to raw-and-honest display, never to a fabricated PMF. History derivations (velocity, jump detection, outcome series) never cross an exclusivity-mode boundary, so a guard transition or band-edge flap can never render as a market move.
exclusivity_guard.reference: core/categorical.js assessExclusivity / buildCategoricalRecord (guard branch); lib/market-history.mjs latestModeSegment

narrative.method: Deterministic, template-based reading composed only from stored fields (median vs 7d/30d-ago, divergence, dominant bucket, shape, dispersion trend, confidence caveat). No language model in the data path; reproducible from narrative_components. Trend claims are suppressed on low-confidence days.
assumptions: Every clause maps to a field in narrative_components; nothing is asserted that is not stored.
narrative.sensitivity_note: Same inputs always produce the same sentence.

analytics_shape.method: Distribution shape from the adjusted CDF: Bowley quartile skewness ((p75-med)-(med-p25))/(p75-p25); a robust fat-tail ratio (10th-90th percentile valuation spread) / IQR vs a normal's 1.90; normalized Shannon entropy and Gini over the density buckets (consensus vs dispersion); dominant bucket.
assumptions: Quantile- and probability-based only; no tail-midpoint assumptions.
analytics_shape.sensitivity_note: Bowley skew and the tail ratio use only interpolated quantiles, so they inherit none of the mean's tail sensitivity.

analytics_dispersion.method: The 25-75% band width (p75-p25) tracked over time; trend = converging when the width is shrinking (growing certainty), diverging when widening.
assumptions: Reads stored historical IQR; no assumptions.
analytics_dispersion.sensitivity_note: A genuine signal: a tightening band means the market is concentrating its view.

analytics_velocity.method: Rate of change of the implied median: 24h/7d/30d changes (the single source for displayed median deltas), 7d/30d annualized drift, and acceleration from the sign of the second difference.
assumptions: Reads stored historical medians; no assumptions.
analytics_velocity.sensitivity_note: All surfaces display the same stored delta values through one rounding helper.

calibration.method: Structural scaffold only. The market resolves once, at IPO close (2027-12-31), so a true calibration / Brier score is impossible before resolution. The standing forecast is recorded so it can be scored later; NO score is computed now.
assumptions: None — explicitly pending resolution.

scenarios.method: TIER 2. Implied share price = market_cap / shares_outstanding, reported as {central, low, high} from the shares range; round-over-round = implied IPO-close median vs the last reported valuation. Each scenario carries its sourced, dated assumption from assumptions.json; with no usable input it renders 'input_required'.
assumptions: shares_outstanding and last_round_valuation are external, press-estimated, low-confidence inputs (SpaceX is private). See assumptions.json and the embedded per-scenario assumptions.
scenarios.sensitivity_note: Quarantined from Tier 1 and validated: no scenario number exists without a sourced+dated assumption; no assumption leaks into derived.market. The published feed uses the registry value; the dashboard lets a user explore their own without mutating the feed.

source_of_record.method: The canonical price is the CLOB /midpoints value = (best_bid + best_ask) / 2 of the live order book. raw_inputs.midpoint (hence every raw_prob and all derived metrics) is this CLOB midpoint. Gamma outcomePrices is a platform-surfaced display price that can lag the book; it is used ONLY for metadata (token ids, volume, threshold) and as a cross-check, never as an input. On disagreement the CLOB midpoint is authoritative and the divergence is reported.
assumptions: None — both inputs are public, auth-free Polymarket endpoints.
source_of_record.sensitivity_note: Accuracy is independently proven by scripts/verify-accuracy.js: dual-source fetch twice, cross-source agreement (±1pt), drift quantification, published-vs-live reconciliation (±2pt + drift) with a separate freshness verdict, and isotonic-validity of the live curve. Report-only; tolerances documented, not tuned to pass.

freshness.method: TIER 1. derived.freshness is a pure function of the snapshot's own fetched_at plus one documented constant (no external input): { as_of, staleness_threshold_hours, stale_after = as_of + threshold, expected_cadence, policy }. The published record carries POLICY ONLY — no frozen age/stale flag, since age is a read-time quantity. Consumers (the dashboard and note) evaluate staleness with a single comparison, now > stale_after, and display an as-of age + stale badge. core/freshness.js is the single source of the policy.
assumptions: None — derived solely from the snapshot's own timestamp.
freshness.sensitivity_note: Threshold = 17h, DERIVED from the snapshot schedule rather than chosen as a literal: the cron (update.yml, '0 0,12,14,16,18,20,22 * * *') runs every 2h 12:00-22:00 UTC plus 00:00, daily incl. weekends, so the largest scheduled gap is the 12h overnight pause (00:00->12:00 UTC). Threshold = 12h max gap + 2h one fully-missed run + 3h Actions queue jitter. A normal overnight pause never flags; anything past 17h is a genuine pipeline failure. core/freshness.js exports the SCHEDULE facts and computes the threshold from them; test/schedule-coupling.test.js re-derives the gaps from the workflow cron so schedule and threshold cannot silently desync. The weekday-only crons are the email runs, not the snapshot.

changelog.change: BUCKET CLASSIFICATION QUORUM (core-fix, shape classification only, preventive — zero live misroutes at fix time). ladderShapeFromMarkets' bucket_pmf check previously used .some() over the 'between' wording alone, so ONE stray 'between' leg reclassified a whole board to bucket_pmf. bucket_pmf now requires a ≥2-leg quorum (the same quorum the touch-verb rule already carries) where each counted leg carries BOTH witnesses: the 'between' wording marker (BUCKET_RE) AND a successful structural interval parse (parseBucketLeg != null). The conjunction — not parse-only — is deliberate and load-bearing: parseBucketLeg's single-bound fallback parses ANY question carrying a money/percent amount ('hit $104' → [104,∞)), so a parse-only quorum would have swallowed every survival ladder into bucket_pmf; the widening-control test locks this permanently. Census at fix time: zero live misroutes (preventive), and every real bucket board passes with margin ≥5 (all carry ≥5 between legs against the quorum of 2). Accepted trade-off: a 1-between minimal bucket board fails the ≥2 quorum and falls to the honest 5.5 chain — unobserved in the wild (census: every real bucket board carries ≥5 between legs); the [shape-tripwire] monotonicity warn is the instrument if one ever appears. Schema unchanged at 2.1.0. Frozen SpaceX replay untouched — parity 4/4 byte-identical.
notes: DISPLAY FIX (no version bump — display semantics only): the resolved-categorical banner now derives its winner label(s) from derived.outcomes' settled-to-1 probabilities (lib/format-detail.mjs resolvedCategoricalWinners), not from lifecycle.resolved_outcome — that side channel carries {threshold, outcome:'Yes'|'No'} with no label, which made every resolved categorical banner read 'resolved: Yes'. lifecycle.resolved_outcome is unchanged and still read wherever else it is used.

OPS FIX (no version bump — backfill status semantics only, preventive, zero live instances at fix time): lib/backfill.mjs backfillMarket previously caught every leg-fetch error and degraded it to history:[], discarding the error signal — so a TOTAL OUTAGE (every leg threw) produced assembled=[] → written=0, failed=0 → status 'done', never retried (the cron's needsBackfill predicate retries only null|'failed'). backfill status gains a terminal 'no_history': assembled=0 with zero leg errors (every leg answered 200 with empty history — a never-traded token, or a board past CLOB's ~Nov-2023 retention horizon) → 'no_history', deliberately excluded from retry. assembled=0 with any leg error → total outage → 'failed' (retryable; the cron self-heals it). Previously both cases were conflated with 'done'. assembled>0 is byte-identical to the pre-existing rule.

SECURITY FIX (no version bump — ops/security only, effective P2, no known active exploit; display and data outputs unchanged): the /api/backfill self-call's destination is now selfBaseUrl() (PUBLIC_APP_URL, falling back to the platform-injected VERCEL_URL), never request-derived. Previously all three self-call sites (addMarket in app/(app)/actions.ts, DetailData's browse-history trigger in components/zones/MarketDetailView.tsx, and the snapshot cron's backfill retry in app/api/snapshot/route.ts) built the fetch target from the request's Host header / x-forwarded-proto / req.url — a header-controlled destination for a fetch carrying the CRON_SECRET Bearer is a credential-egress surface, closed regardless of whether Vercel's edge happens to reject a mismatched Host today. triggerBackfill(id, host, proto) is now triggerBackfill(id) — the removed parameters ARE the fix, not merely unused. Unset base fails closed with a logged skip (reason 'no configured base url'), matching the existing CRON_SECRET-unset skip. The 202-ack + dedicated-300s decoupling (backfill runs on its own budget, not the caller's) is untouched.

changelog.change: INSUFFICIENT-OUTCOMES GUARD (core-fix, categorical only, preventive — zero live instances at fix time). assessExclusivity's degenerate branch (fewer than 2 placeholder-filtered priced real legs) previously returned verdict 'exclusive' — the UNGUARDED path — so a single real leg fell straight into normalizeProbabilities([p]), which always returns [1.0]: a lone 30% leg displayed as a fabricated 100%-certain winner (dominant_outcome, implied_winner, consensus HIGH, entropy 0, and Increment B's consensus reliability lift all following from that fabricated certainty). The branch now returns verdict 'insufficient_outcomes' at the SAME branch position (first check, before the nested/sum tests — the RT branch-order property is unaffected since none of those paths reach fewer than 2 priced legs) and routes to the existing guarded raw-display path: outcomes carry raw_probability only (no probability/dominant_*/entropy/consensus_strength/implied_winner keys), and the narrative reads 'Only one real outcome carries a price — a single outcome cannot form a distribution.' Consumer sweep: every reader of exclusivity.verdict is either `!== 'exclusive'`-gated or value-agnostic, and no schema constrains the verdict enum — a new verdict value suppresses the PMF everywhere by construction, with no other file requiring a change beyond the categorical-verdict TS union and the ShapeNotice label switch. Schema unchanged at 2.1.0. Frozen SpaceX replay untouched (not categorical) — parity 4/4 byte-identical.

LAST-TRADE WITNESS GUARD (core-fix, ALL 5 shape fetchers via the single choke point fetchLastTradePrice; live prod finding: CLOB's /last-trade-price endpoint fabricates {"price":"0.5","side":""} for a never-traded token with no order book — the fingerprint is side:"" ⇔ never-traded; a genuine trade always carries side "buy"/"sell", including 8 real trades that landed at exactly 0.5, so price can never be the discriminator, only side). fetchLastTradePrice now treats a last-trade response as an observation ONLY when side is 'buy' or 'sell' (case-insensitive); any other side (empty, missing, or unrecognized) returns null and logs one greppable warn ([last-trade] fabricated (side:"")) — but only when a price was actually present to fabricate (a fetch error or empty body keeps the prior silent-null path, unchanged). null flows into each caller's EXISTING skip machinery (skippedThresholds / midpoint_fallback.skippedCount) unmodified — this is a skip, never a price substitution, and no caller or pricing tier was reordered. General witness principle this confirms (see decisions.md): a CLOB scalar is an observation only when its structural witness is present — a two-sided book for a midpoint (1.10.0), a side for a trade (this fix). Population measured at fix time: 369 fabricated last-trade legs across 15 boards, 4 display-visible on filterless ladders. Frozen SpaceX replay untouched (no last-trade legs in the frozen record) — parity 4/4 byte-identical.

RESOLVED TRANSITIONS STORE SETTLED TRUTH (behavior change, ALL 5 shapes; live prod finding: a resolved-transition freeze was a silent no-op — freezePriorRecord kept the prior's fetched_at, and the market_snapshots upsert on (market_id, fetched_at) with ignoreDuplicates silently dropped the RESOLVED row, leaving the market OPEN in the cache forever — victims world-cup-winner, which-continent-will-win-the-world-cup). A RESOLVED transition with a cached prior now ALWAYS tries settled truth first (append, new fetched_at — a genuine write, not a same-key upsert), via the same buildMinimalResolvedRecord the no-prior first-browse path already used. Freeze is now degraded-fallback ONLY (no leg has a parseable settled price), logged loud (never a silent fallback), and any freeze that keeps the prior's fetched_at (the degraded freeze, or a CLOSED_PENDING-with-prior freeze) now writes with replace:true so the lifecycle stamp cannot silently no-op again. A resolution transition also stamps ONE final history row (source='transition'); jump/velocity/headline-change/biggest-movers derivations now exclude that row from narration (the settlement is a real step, not a market move) while the chart series still renders it. writeRecord's snapshot upsert now throws loud on ANY undeclared silent conflict (replace:false + zero affected rows), independent of this fix's own paths. Schema unchanged at 2.1.0. SpaceX reference record is grandfathered as the historical artifact of the freeze-epoch semantic — it is stored RESOLVED and serves via SERVE_FINAL, structurally never re-entering this path; its raw_sha256 is untouched. Frozen SpaceX replay untouched — parity 4/4 byte-identical.

SETTLED-LEG PRICING (behavior change, ALL multi-leg shapes; live prod finding: Norway, eliminated and UMA-resolved-NO, displayed at 50% because CLOB's midpoint endpoint fabricates 0.5 over an EMPTY book — /prices returns sentinels BUY=0/SELL=1 for absent sides and midpoint averages them). The per-leg pricing chain (core/fetch.js priceLeg, ONE definition for every fetcher) now prices by most-settled-truth-first: (1) SETTLED (umaResolutionStatus='resolved' + parseable settled price via the shared settledYesStr reader, label-aligned, null-not-zero) → the leg's own settled YES price, midpoint_source 'resolved_settlement', bid/ask null; (2) PENDING (closed / not accepting orders, not yet resolved) → last_trade, NEVER the midpoint (dead book); (3) OPEN → midpoint only over a LIVE TWO-SIDED book (sentinel sides are stripped as absences; a one-sided book is never read as live), then the existing bid/ask/last-trade tiers. outcomePrices on an OPEN leg mirrors LIVE prices and is never read as settled. raw_inputs now carry the settled string for settled legs → new hashes going forward (the hash is over observed truth; the settled price IS the observation). Schema unchanged at 2.1.0 (no shape change; 'resolved_settlement' was already a valid midpoint_source). Frozen SpaceX replay untouched — parity 4/4 byte-identical immediately post-change.

EXCLUSIVITY GUARD HARDENING (behavior change, categorical only; red-team INC 7, two confirmed fabrication paths closed). (1) NO FALL-THROUGH: a dated-dominated board (≥0.8 'by <date>' legs) with ≥2 DISTINCT deadlines never reaches the sum test — monotone ⇒ nested_deadline, non-monotone (stale-quote inversion > 2.5pp eps) ⇒ ambiguous/raw. Previously an in-band sum de-vigged such a CDF into a fabricated PMF (RT-2). Boards whose dated legs share ONE deadline (common suffix, e.g. every leg '…by 2027?') still fall through — there the deadline is not the differentiator, and genuinely exclusive boards keep their honest de-vig. (2) parseByDeadline now parses numeric ('by 6/30/2026') and quarter ('by Q3 2026') deadlines — previously every such leg collapsed to the bare-year fallback's IDENTICAL key, blinding the distinct-deadline requirement (RT-1); ordinal days no longer eat the year ('by July 4th, 2026', RT-3). Every verdict flip this causes degrades toward raw-and-honest, never toward the de-vig. Schema unchanged at 2.1.0 (no contract shape change). SpaceX parity 4/4 byte-identical.

EXCLUSIVITY GUARD (behavior change, categorical only). The de-vig no longer runs unconditionally: boards classified NESTED_DEADLINE / NON_EXCLUSIVE / AMBIGUOUS (see metrics.categorical.exclusivity_guard) display RAW observed prices with all PMF derivations suppressed and an explicit structure notice. Schema: the categorical derived contract becomes conditional (exclusivity block XOR the PMF field set) — schema_version 2.0.0 → 2.1.0 (AMENDED 2026-07-13, operator ruling; supersedes this entry's original 'unchanged at 2.0.0'). Rationale: a consumer reading dominant_prob now gets undefined where a number was previously guaranteed — the contract materially changed, and a version that stands still while its contract moves is not a signal. The bump is parity-safe: the parity gate asserts only the raw-inputs hash and derived deep-equality; schema_version is top-level and in neither, and the frozen RESOLVED SpaceX record is never re-stamped (resolution guard skips the pipeline). Survival/binary/touch/bucket paths untouched; SpaceX parity 4/4 byte-identical.

DOCUMENTATION ONLY — no formula, threshold, or schema change. Wrote down four rules that existed only in code: (1) the 0.5% MATERIAL_ADJUSTMENT immateriality threshold on isotonic tweaks (metrics.confidence.material_adjustment); (2) the $2K 24h floor on the 7d-volume HIGH path (metrics.confidence.windowed_volume_floor); (3) the CORRECTED book_depth selection — dominant-outcome leg, max-fallback — superseding the 1.7.0 entry's 'max per-leg' wording (red-team F1) (metrics.confidence.book_depth_selection); (4) the categorical placeholder-leg filter applied before de-vig (metrics.categorical.placeholder_filter).

Order-book DEPTH → LIQUIDITY (Increment C), additive + parity-safe (no schema change). Gamma exposes a per-market `liquidity` field ($ of resting orders) in the SAME meta response already fetched; we record the MAX per-leg value as derived.liquidity.book_depth (max, NOT a sum — resting orders don't aggregate across mutually-exclusive legs). It is SUPPLEMENTARY (outside raw_inputs, never hashed) and OMITTED when absent (resolved markets carry no liquidity field → SpaceX frozen replay byte-identical, parity 4/4). bookDepthSignal tiers (operator-calibrated against ~150 live markets, max per-leg depth): HIGH ≥ $100K (move real size), MED ≥ $10K (usable), LOW below (thin). It feeds the LIQUIDITY dimension of all 4 scorers WORST-OF with windowed volume — so a thin book caps liquidity even when recent volume is high (e.g. $3M/24h volume + a $5K book → LIQUIDITY LOW: you can't transact at size). Depth never affects RELIABILITY. Surfaced in VolumeCard ('book $X') + the liquidity basis chips. ⚠ RED-TEAM TODO: the $100K/$10K depth cutoffs (with Increment B's entropy 0.40 / leader 0.70 / rel-spread 0.50).

Consensus/decisiveness → RELIABILITY (Increment B), additive (no schema change; confidence shape unchanged). CATEGORICAL: a strongly-concentrated distribution (normalized entropy ≤ 0.40 AND a ≥70% leader) LIFTS a spread-driven 'medium' reliability to 'high' — the headline outcome is a well-formed agreement, reliable even when long-tail legs have wider books (the mean-spread averaging that depressed it isn't what the headline rests on). It never overrides a genuine defect: a >8% averaged book stays 'low', and a missing/last-trade outcome still caps. BINARY: a decisive probability (≤0.02 or ≥0.98) whose spread is a MINORITY of the smaller tail (≤50%) adds a 'price well-determined' reliability basis; there is NO tier lift for binary (a single book has no wide-tail-leg averaging to correct, and a medium-band spread on an extreme line always dominates the tiny tail). Sharpens the CT-Governor case: 98% consensus now reads reliability HIGH explicitly, independent of its (low) liquidity. Ladder/touch unchanged; SpaceX parity 4/4 byte-identical (categorical/binary-only).

Confidence SPLIT into two independent dimensions (Increment A), NO change to the underlying signals/thresholds — they are REPARTITIONED, not retuned. derived.confidence is now { reliability, liquidity }, each a {tier,score,reasons}. RELIABILITY (is the displayed number trustworthy) owns: threshold count, monotonicity, spread (+expiry tolerance), last-trade fallback, missing rungs, stale feed. LIQUIDITY (can you transact at this price) owns: book-thin breadth, windowed volume (all-time fallback), closed/not-accepting-orders rungs, liquidity drop. The two are orthogonal — a market can be HIGH reliability + LOW liquidity (strong consensus, nobody trading) or the reverse. The old single tier is recoverable as worst(reliability, liquidity). Schema 2.0.0 (BREAKING: confidence shape). SpaceX frozen output: reliability HIGH + liquidity HIGH; the parity gate's faithfulness proof asserts reliability.tier === the frozen single tier, worst(reliability,liquidity) === it, and the two reason lists' union === the frozen reasons.

Multi-market generalization (Phase 1), NO formula change. Every market-specific value (tail offsets, mean-sensitivity grid, liquidity floor, confidence count thresholds, dispersion/accel eps, density label unit, tracked thresholds, narrative wording, calibration date, asset metadata) moved into a per-market MarketConfig (core/markets/*.json); the pipeline now processes any threshold-ladder event, not just SpaceX. SpaceX's config pins the exact prior constants, so its output is byte-identical (proven by a blocking parity gate: raw_sha256 + full derived block + 183-day history). Added a two-stage market-resolution lifecycle (snapshot.lifecycle: OPEN / CLOSED_PENDING / RESOLVED) — a resolved market is frozen and never re-pulled, a closed-but-unconfirmed market claims no final outcome, and a non-OPEN market is final (not flagged stale). Tier-2 scenarios are now optional (attached only when a market registers an assumptions file); the firewall is unchanged. Schema 1.3.0 (additive: snapshot.lifecycle; derived.scenarios optional; assumptions_version nullable).

Cadence + freshness policy change, NO formula change. Snapshot cadence raised from 1/day (14:00 UTC) to every 2h 12:00-00:00 UTC (7/day, overnight pause 00:00-12:00 UTC); email crons unchanged. Staleness threshold re-derived as a function of the schedule (12h max scheduled gap + 2h one missed run + 3h queue jitter = 17h, was a 50h literal sized for the daily cadence) — core/freshness.js now exports the SCHEDULE facts and computes the threshold from them, with a coupling test re-deriving the gaps from the workflow cron. Added a post-publish accuracy verify step in CI (publish-then-alert: scripts/verify-accuracy.js runs non-strict after every push; a FAIL marks the run red but never blocks publication or emails). Minor bump: published policy fields (staleness_threshold_hours, expected_cadence, policy) change meaning for consumers; no metric formula or schema shape changed.

Added Tier-1 derived.freshness (as-of anchor + absolute stale_after; 50h threshold sized to the daily cron) surfaced as an as-of age + stale badge on the dashboard and note. Schema 1.2.1 (additive: derived.freshness). No change to any published metric value.
